newsitem.title: INDIA: PanAmSat to beam Star DTH TV into India.
newsitem.headline: PanAmSat to beam Star DTH TV into India.

text.p: PanAmSat Corp said on Wednesday its PAS-4 Indian Ocean region satellite would serve as the transmission platform for News Corp subsidiary Star TV's new direct-to-home (DTH) television service in India.
The new Star TV service, called Sky, will use seven Ku-band transponders on the PAS-4 satellite which is capable of beaming dozens of television channels to subscribers in India using rooftop dishes.

"With the major addition of Star TV, PanAmSat's customers have clearly established PAS-4 as the leading broadcast satellite in south Asia," Frederick Landman, PanAmSat president and chief executive officer said in a statement.
The statement said PanAmSat has conducted extensive tests of PAS-4's ability to provide high quality DTH transmissions to India in all weather conditions.

PAS-4, launched in August 1995, is located at 68.5 degrees east longitude and contains 16 C-band and 24 Ku-band transponders. The satellite is also the transmission platform for DTH services in South Africa and the Middle East and delivers more than two dozen TV channels to cable systems in south Asia.

Last week the Greenwich, Conn.-based satellite company said it expects a delay in completion and delivery of its PAS-7 Indian Ocean satellite. The launch, previously scheduled for late 1997, has been delayed to the first quarter of 1998.
